conflicts.description: The manual's switch-matrix chart and Switch Part Numbers table print 22 'Hat Target Bottom' and 24 'Hat Target Top', and its switch-location drawing reads the three stacked hat-target callouts top to bottom as 24, 23, 22 (the second digit of the top callout hidden under a leader line). The ROM's Active Switch Test names 22 'TOP HAT TARGET' and 24 'BOTTOM HAT TARGET' with the same wires (WHT-BLU and WHT-GRY returns), the game lights the Top Hat Target lamp 57 when 22 closes, and the retained table pulses 22 from its top target and 24 from its bottom one. A recreation consumes the answer as the physical position of each switch. Labels follow the ROM and the placements follow the table, both marked conflicted. Resolution path: on a physical machine, hit the top hat target in the Active Switch Test and read the switch number, or trace the WHT-BLU row-6 return (CN10-3) to the target it reaches.

Both names denote what PinMAME publishes here, the left cabinet flipper button: the game data declares FLIP1516 = FLIP_SWNO(15,16) with no FLIP_SOL, so PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine, and core.c's core_updateSw rewrites this switch on every update from PinMAME's flipper-column button bit 84. The retained table writes 15 itself from the left flipper key before handing the key to de.vbs, which writes 84 (Rab_KeyUp/RaB_KeyDown, script lines 353 and 371); PinMAME rewrites 15 from 84 on its next update, so such a write cannot be held. ROM evidence (3.20 Active Switch Test): a host write of 1 to public 15 showed 'LEFT FLIPPER', wires GRN-RED WHT-VIO and '#15' but fired no flipper output, while holding 84 showed the same frame and fired 47/48; with every public switch at 0 the screen shows NONE. Coin-door diagnostic button, named 'Black Button' by s11.h's DE_COMPORTS and placed in switch column 0 rather than the playfield matrix; Data East defines only these two (DE_SWADVANCE -7, DE_SWUPDN -6). inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP1516 = FLIP_SWNO(15,16) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8. ROM evidence: holding this address at 1 in the 3.20 Active Switch Test shows NONE.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP1516 = FLIP_SWNO(15,16) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 16 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 16: a host write to 16 is overwritten on the next update. The retained known-working script drives it: Rab_KeyUp/RaB_KeyDown hand the right flipper key to de.vbs vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp (script lines 355 and 373), which set Controller.Switch(swLRFlip) with swLRFlip = 82 (excerpt vpm-script-library-flippers). The physical counterpart is the right cabinet flipper button. ROM evidence (3.20 Active Switch Test): holding public 82 at 1 shows 'RIGHT FLIPPER', the wires GRN-RED WHT-GRY and '#16', the matrix switch core_updateSw copies it into, while the other six flipper-column addresses (81, 83 and 85-88) show NONE, so the ROM cannot see them. Contact: the manual's Flipper Solenoids table routes the flipper ground 'ORN-VIO CPU CN19-1' through the cabinet flipper switch to the flipper board ('BLU-VIO CN1-1'). A switch in series with the flipper's ground energises the coil while it is closed, so the released button rests open; public 1 is the pressed button.

machine.name: Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle and Friends

mechanisms.behavior: The Outhole Assy (500-5082-00) on drive 1 kicks a drained ball from the outhole switch 10 into a three-ball trough (11 left, 12 center, 13 right, the release position), and the Ball Feed Assy (Trough Eject, 500-5012-01) on drive 2 kicks the ball at 13 into the shooter lane, where switch 14 senses it. ROM evidence (3.20 game start, the host moving the balls): with balls on 11-13 the ROM pulsed the Trough Eject 8 times after Start while 13 stayed closed and 0 times while the served ball rested on 14; it pulsed the Outhole 3 times while a drained ball held 10 closed, and once that ball reached 11 it pulsed the Trough Eject 5 times to serve the next ball. The host moved every ball, so the counts are the ROM's retries, not travel times. The retained table rests its balls on three trough kickers and kicks them on the same two solenoids.
mechanisms.label: Outhole, Three-Ball Trough and Trough Eject

mechanisms.behavior: The Ball Launch Assy (500-5477-01) on drive 16, through the PPB booster at 50 V, launches the ball waiting on the shooter lane switch 14 when the player presses the cabinet Launch Button 9. Adjustment 47 (Trigger Enabled) lets the button fire the launcher during the Bomb Fuse animation. ROM evidence (3.20 game start): with the ball on 14 the ROM fired nothing until the Launch Button was pressed, which fired [16]. The retained table fires a cvpmImpulseP auto-plunger on its swPlunger trigger from the solenoid.
mechanisms.label: Auto Launch

mechanisms.behavior: The Kick Back Assembly (500-5080-00) on switched solenoid 22, 23-800 through a PPB booster at 50 V, kicks a ball back out of the left outlane. The Game Specific Features page says return-lane rollovers raise the Laser Kick value and the right orbit relights and collects it. ROM evidence (3.20 Laser Kick Test): closing the left outlane switch 32 fires public 22. The retained table arms its LaserKick kicker only while 22 is on.
mechanisms.label: Laser Kick (Left Outlane Kickback)

mechanisms.behavior: The Super VUK (500-5116-04, balloon boxed on the left rail) on drive 5, through a PPB booster at 50 V, raises the ball from switch 29. ROM evidence (3.20 Laser Kick Test): closing 29 fires public 5. In the retained table the Under Trough switch 37 sits in a subway entered from the playfield that delivers the ball to the Super VUK; that routing is the table's model, and no ROM run tied 37 to 5.
mechanisms.label: Super VUK (Left Rail)

mechanisms.behavior: The Vertical Up Kicker (500-5326-00) on drive 4, through a PPB booster at 50 V, raises the ball from the Hat Trick hole (switch 52) at the upper left onto the VUK Ramp (535-6363-00). ROM evidence (3.20): the Laser Kick Test fires public 4 from 52, and in the Hat Trick probes the ROM kicked 1.9-2.1 s after 52 closed.
mechanisms.label: Playfield VUK (Hat Trick Hole)

mechanisms.behavior: The Playfield Diverter coil (drive 13, 23-800) diverts a ball rolling up the left orbit into the Hat Trick hole while Hat Trick is lit. No switch reports its position. ROM evidence (3.20 Hat Trick probes): the ROM turned 13 on as the ball passed the left orbit bottom switch 33, held it about 0.8 s and dropped it 0.2-0.3 s after the hole switch 52 closed, so the diverter is a held output. The retained table swings its diverter while 13 is on. Which of the two Diverter Assemblies in the Major Assemblies list (items 15 and 16) this coil moves is not stated.
mechanisms.label: Playfield Diverter (Left Orbit to the Hat Trick Hole)

mechanisms.behavior: The Ramp Diverter coil (drive 12, 27-1400) moves a ramp diverter at the upper left. No switch reports its position, and no retained run exercised it in a game. The retained table swings its diverter open while 12 is on and back when it turns off.
mechanisms.label: Ramp Diverter

mechanisms.behavior: The Gate Lift Coil (515-5711-00, drive 14, 31-1800) lifts a control gate at the top centre of the playfield. No switch reports its position, and no retained run exercised it in a game. The retained table makes its gate non-collidable while 14 is on.
mechanisms.label: Top Control Gate

mechanisms.behavior: The 5 Bank Drop Target Assy (500-5621-05) on the right of the playfield: targets 17 (top) to 21 (bottom), reset together by drive 15 (22-600). ROM evidence (3.20 Save Nell probes): with all five held down after a completed bank, the ROM pulsed the reset coil 3 times; a recreation should raise the bank on each pulse and expect the ROM to retry while a switch stays closed.
mechanisms.label: Five-Bank Drop Targets

mechanisms.behavior: Three Turbo Bumper Assys (500-5227-00) sensed at 44-46 (part 180-5015-00) and fired by switched solenoids 17-19 (23-800). The center bumper is the lower one between the other two. ROM evidence (3.20, a game in play): closing 44, 45 and 46 fires 17, 18 and 19, and the ROM names them LEFT, CENTER and RIGHT.

mechanisms.behavior: IPDB describes a mechanical backbox animation in which Bullwinkle pulls Rocky, a rhino or a lion out of his hat; the coils on drives 3 (Lion), 6 (Rocky) and 7 (Rhino) sit in the backbox. The Game Specific Features page: shooting the left orbit into the hole while Hat Trick is lit lets Bullwinkle pull an animal out of his hat; Rocky lights Extra Ball, Rhino starts the Rhino Bonus countdown and Lion starts the Jackpot. ROM evidence (3.20 Hat Trick probes): about 0.1 s after the left orbit top switch 34 closed, the ROM energised one figure coil; on the first award of a figure it held the coil 1.0 s, then switched it on again for 0.5 s starting just before the VUK fired, and a repeated award of the same figure held it once for 0.3 s. Awards 1 and 2 used the Lion (Jackpot lamp 54 flashing afterwards), awards 3 and 4 the Rhino (Rhino Bonus lamp 61); Rocky was not awarded. The figures' physical motion, travel and return are not documented in any retained source; the retained table animates a figure up while its coil is on and down when it turns off.
mechanisms.label: Backbox Hat Trick Figures

mechanisms.behavior: Nell's Log Assembly (500-5638-00, beside the drop-target bank) is a motor driving a saw disc through an O-ring belt and a gear rack under a log carrier; the Relay Board 520-5010-00 switches 28 VAC to the motor while solenoid 9 is on. No switch reports its position, and how the carrier returns is not legible on the assembly drawing. The Game Specific Features page: completing the drop targets advances a value 5-4-3-2-1, the Nell timer starts when all lamps flash, and hitting drop targets saves Nell before time expires; Adjustment 51 (Any Drop Wins Nell) chooses between any drop target and the whole bank. ROM evidence (3.20 Save Nell probes): the ROM switched 9 on 0.2 s after the second completed bank (not after the first) and held it 14.5 s until a drop-target hit saved Nell (dropping it 0.2 s after the hit), and 18.1 s when nothing was hit. The two retained recreation lineages disagree on the travel: one swings the log back and forth while 9 is on and stops it in place when 9 turns off, the other moves it one way while 9 is on and back when 9 turns off.
mechanisms.label: Save Nell (Nell's Log and Saw)

Power and hold therefore assert and release together and are not independently controllable; a recreation must not model them as two coils. The right flipper's power cell prints CN1-1, the same pin as its switch line; both are literal, and the pin is recorded as printed. The retained table binds nothing to 45.
